cards.blocked_on_pharos: Expose explicit timezone-derived civil hour and weekday or implement the admitted time-bucket profile.
cards.calculation_gap: Human message timestamps and typed words are available, but local hour/day-of-week grouping fields and heatmap display are absent.
cards.performance_note: Aggregate message-time facts with index-friendly range filters; a display timezone alone does not implement local-hour grouping.

cards.title: Where does my attention switch most often?
cards.recipe: Order genuine human messages by time and canonical repository; count repository switches and show runs, with configurable gaps separating visits.
cards.preview: Colored repository ribbons across a day.
cards.eligibility: Timestamps and stable repository identity; message switches are a proxy for attention, not complete human activity.
cards.destination: Human-message sequences and repository switches.
cards.exploration_value: Makes fragmented collaboration visible without guessing what happened off-screen.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Create human-message visit/switch events with stable cross-conversation ordering and an explicit gap rule.
cards.calculation_gap: writing_messages can order by sent_at/repository but cannot count transitions or define gap-separated visits as metrics.
cards.performance_note: Use a timestamp-ordered human event stream; materialize switch facts incrementally for frequent previews.

cards.title: How much agent work overlaps?
cards.recipe: Build observed agent-run intervals and compute concurrency over time; distinguish complete intervals, event-active estimates and missing ends.
cards.preview: Layered active lanes with a small concurrency curve.
cards.eligibility: Usable run timestamps and interval definitions; overlapping time is not automatically time saved.
cards.destination: Runs contributing to each overlapping interval.
cards.exploration_value: Shows the scale and shape of parallel work.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Publish observed run intervals with missing-end coverage and event-active estimation labels.
cards.calculation_gap: Agent sessions/activity are retained, but reliable intervals and concurrency reductions are not Query Table metrics.
cards.performance_note: Union/sweep interval endpoints and bucket occupancy; do not sum durations or infer time saved from overlap.

cards.title: Which tasks disappear and then resume?
cards.recipe: Find conversation or work resumes after long observed gaps; show the restart request and subsequent rereads or clarifications.
cards.preview: A split timeline with the restart excerpt bridging the gap.
cards.eligibility: Retained resumed activity on the same canonical work; silence alone is not abandonment.
cards.destination: Resumed work, gaps and events around restart.
cards.exploration_value: Helps recover interrupted work and inspect restart overhead.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Materialize resume episodes and their restart messages/read/clarification facts.
cards.calculation_gap: Work activity dates identify recent work, while restart gaps and surrounding events require stream-level sequencing.
cards.performance_note: Partition by canonical work/stream and query stored gap episodes; no activity after a gap does not establish abandonment.

cards.title: What is the path from request to observed finish?
cards.recipe: Sequence request, orientation, edit, verification and explicit finish milestones; group common paths and measure elapsed intervals with idle gaps visible.
cards.preview: A compact journey strip with a large gap or recurring loop emphasized.
cards.eligibility: Retained milestones; durations remain elapsed spans rather than continuous effort.
cards.destination: Work journeys and the evidence supporting each milestone.
cards.exploration_value: Makes complex workflows understandable at a glance.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Build request/orientation/edit/check/finish milestone facts with explicit elapsed spans, idle gaps and missing stages.
cards.calculation_gap: Isolated edit/test/outcome fields exist but no complete milestone journey relation is exposed.
cards.performance_note: Query prepared journey rows; ordering and completion semantics belong to the host, while generic rendering could be extensible.

cards.title: Where do approvals hold up recorded workflows?
cards.recipe: Pair explicit permission requests with approvals, rejections and subsequent continuation; summarize observed delay by action and harness.
cards.preview: A request-to-approval interval with its action label.
cards.eligibility: Paired permission events and usable timestamps; generic tool timestamp gaps do not prove approval wait.
cards.destination: Permission episodes and continuation evidence.
cards.exploration_value: Finds avoidable interruption patterns when the transcript supports them.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Extract permission episodes per harness and retain explicit pairing and duration source.
cards.calculation_gap: Rejection/error classes exist, but paired permission request, response and continuation timestamps are not standardized.
cards.performance_note: Only explicit paired events measure approval waiting; timestamp-derived tool gaps must not be silently repurposed.

cards.title: Are my conversation rounds getting longer?
cards.recipe: Count actions and genuine exchanges per conversation round; compare matched distributions with the preceding window and inspect long-tail sessions.
cards.preview: Two small distributions with examples from the tail.
cards.eligibility: A stable round definition and comparable populations; do not interpret fewer human messages as better automatically.
cards.destination: Round-level events and their conversations.
cards.exploration_value: Helps users notice changes in interaction style over time.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Derive genuine exchange rounds and action-run facts with comparable prior-window coverage.
cards.calculation_gap: Work-level turn counts exist but conversation-round definitions and per-round action counts are absent.
cards.performance_note: Analyze a prepared round population; a second grouped-distribution stage is useful when starting from raw events.

cards.title: How much time is tool work versus gaps between events?
cards.recipe: Union overlapping timed tool intervals within each stream; compare with observed session spans and label remaining gaps without assigning them to thinking or human work.
cards.preview: A timeline with timed calls and unclassified gaps.
cards.eligibility: Complete timed intervals and explicit coverage; never sum parallel durations as elapsed wall time.
cards.destination: Timed calls, overlap handling and unclassified intervals.
cards.exploration_value: Helps inspect workflow timing without inventing hidden activity.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Publish timed intervals, observed spans and coverage at stream grain, or materialize union length and unclassified gaps.
cards.calculation_gap: Per-call timings can be summed but that gives incorrect elapsed time for overlap; session span completeness also varies.
cards.performance_note: Union overlap before computing fractions; open intervals and missing timings remain unknown.

cards.title: Which workflows would I happily repeat?
cards.recipe: Find work with explicit positive acceptance, usable verification, modest human steering and reusable task structure; show each criterion separately.
cards.preview: Starting prompt paired with acceptance evidence and a short workflow trace.
cards.eligibility: Supported acceptance and relevant verification; avoid a single opaque success score.
cards.destination: Candidate workflows with criteria and source passages.
cards.exploration_value: Offers positive examples the user can collect as future starting points.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Prepare evidence-backed workflow criteria and source passages; preserve separate criteria instead of an opaque success score.
cards.calculation_gap: Work outcomes and writing can provide candidates, but explicit acceptance, relevant verification and reusable structure are not complete joined facts.
cards.performance_note: Query stored criteria at canonical work grain; recommendations and judgments are Pharos product logic.

cards.title: Which recoveries are worth learning from?
cards.recipe: Rank failure-to-recovery episodes by recurrence, changed strategy and explicit observed resolution; show the pivotal changed call or instruction.
cards.preview: Failure fragment, pivotal action and observed recovery in three frames.
cards.eligibility: A retained failure and comparable successful follow-up; causal wording needs more than sequence alone.
cards.destination: Complete recovery episodes and their pivotal evidence.
cards.exploration_value: Turns mistakes into a library of useful techniques.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Publish recurring recovery episodes with resolution evidence and action-difference annotations.
cards.calculation_gap: Raw failures and later calls exist, but linked recovery episodes and the pivotal changed action do not.
cards.performance_note: Rank indexed episode facts by recurrence and useful evidence; don't rerun transcript sequence extraction for every refresh.

cards.title: Which improvements stayed improved?
cards.recipe: Join recorded fixes or findings to before-and-after failure exposure; inspect recurrence over successive windows and include confidence or small-sample labels.
cards.preview: A before-and-after rate trace with the fix date.
cards.eligibility: Dated fix and compatible ongoing exposure; absence of recurrence with no exposure is not success.
cards.destination: Fix evidence, relevant failures and observation denominators.
cards.exploration_value: Helps users understand which interventions are holding up.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Expose fix/measurement and relevant call-population facts with observation coverage.
cards.calculation_gap: Pharos has findings and metric evidence below the table, but dated fixes plus compatible exposure/recurrence periods are not a registered source.
cards.performance_note: Reuse host measurement facts and period rollups; no recurrence with no exposure must not look like a successful fix.

cards.title: What new kinds of work am I trying?
cards.recipe: Classify requests into task families and compare with the preceding window; show newly observed families with representative requests.
cards.preview: Three request fragments with small first-observed timeline marks.
cards.eligibility: Task-family evidence and enough earlier coverage; do not claim first-ever activity from a short archive.
cards.destination: Work in the newly observed families.
cards.exploration_value: Encourages exploration and reflects expanding capability.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Materialize versioned task-family labels and representative requests, including multi-label membership semantics.
cards.calculation_gap: Purpose summaries offer text but not a stable task-family taxonomy with prior-window coverage.
cards.performance_note: Query label membership and aligned counts; reclassification revisions must invalidate cached comparisons.

cards.title: What combinations of tools are unusual for me?
cards.recipe: Build ordered workflow motifs within streams; compare recent sequences with the preceding window and surface supported uncommon combinations.
cards.preview: A novel three-tool path with a representative result fragment.
cards.eligibility: A valid recent motif and sufficient prior sequence coverage; novelty is not superiority.
cards.destination: Sessions containing the motif and their outcomes.
cards.exploration_value: Gives the conveyor surprising, concrete discoveries beyond top-N rankings.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Produce bounded typed workflow motifs and marginal frequencies at stream grain.
cards.calculation_gap: Tool categories can be counted but ordered motifs and personal historical rarity are not fields.
cards.performance_note: Cap motif length and minimum support; avoid unbounded sequence mining or all-history rescans.

cards.title: What is the playbook for a new repository?
cards.recipe: Detect recently observed repositories and summarize evidenced recurring setup commands, test commands, documentation sources and early obstacles.
cards.preview: A tiny repository map with two real commands and one source.
cards.eligibility: Several retained sessions in a newly observed repository; distinguish common actions from recommended best practice.
cards.destination: The repository's startup work and supporting events.
cards.exploration_value: Turns the user's recent experience into a useful orientation view.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Build repository orientation facts with actual setup/test/source examples and explicit recently-observed status.
cards.calculation_gap: Repository commands, domains and first observed activity can be selected; an evidenced playbook involves extraction and interpretation.
cards.performance_note: Aggregate prepared repository events and hydrate a few examples; do not equate frequency with best practice.

cards.title: What deserves a reusable instruction or skill?
cards.recipe: Combine repeated human instructions, recurring recovery procedures and reused examples; rank candidate procedures by recurrence and explicit successful use.
cards.preview: Repeated rule plus two short evidenced workflow steps.
cards.eligibility: A repeatable procedure with inspectable evidence; suggestions require human judgment before becoming instructions.
cards.destination: Candidate procedures, repeated requests and observed outcomes.
cards.exploration_value: Connects exploration to durable improvements in the user's toolkit.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Combine instruction/recovery/example annotations into candidate reusable procedures with evidence links.
cards.calculation_gap: Repeated rules, procedures and their explicit successful use are not normalized evidence relations.
cards.performance_note: This is a Pharos extractor/recommendation workflow; Query Table can filter and group its saved candidate facts.

cards.title: What would I miss in an average?
cards.recipe: For distributions already supported by the data surface bimodality, a concentrated tail or cohort reversals; show the grouped and ungrouped views together.
cards.preview: Overall distribution beside two differently shaped cohorts.
cards.eligibility: Enough observations per cohort and a clear supported feature; avoid unstable statistical discoveries from tiny samples.
cards.destination: Full distributions, cohort definitions and the observations behind them.
cards.exploration_value: Exposes the power of complex aggregation through a surprising but inspectable view.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Supply correct-grain populations/cohort labels and a supported feature detector; a manually chosen distribution can ship without automated claims.
cards.calculation_gap: v2 box/histogram can expose distributions, but detecting bimodality or cohort reversals needs statistical interpretation and compatible cohorts.
cards.performance_note: Use shared bins and support gates; do not infer robust surprises from a sparse population or different bin extents.

query_table_requests.title: Filter evaluated row values before paging
query_table_requests.gap: Server computed fields support selection/order/measure/group, while computed WHERE remains deferred.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add capability-gated typed predicates over server-evaluated fields before total counts, page selection and all-matching metrics; retain unsupported clauses with diagnostics.
query_table_requests.performance: Push predicates into the authoritative relation; stable host projections or expression indexes may help measured hot definitions. Page-local filtering is incorrect.

query_table_requests.title: Filter grouped results before ranking and limiting
query_table_requests.gap: Metrics can order and limit groups, but have no HAVING/result predicate.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add validated aggregate-result predicates such as distinct conversations >= 3, observations >= 20, failures > 0 and rate > threshold. Evaluate before result LIMIT and expose final group count.
query_table_requests.performance: Filter before top-K. Client filtering of a capped group list can miss eligible groups and produce incorrect recommendations.

query_table_requests.title: Reduce grouped results in a second explicit stage
query_table_requests.gap: Aggregate formulas have one input relation and one grouping step. Box/histogram inputs are individual rows; nested aggregates are rejected.
query_table_requests.proposal: Support a bounded group → typed result relation → project/filter → second reduction pipeline. Example: sum usage per conversation, then histogram those totals by repository. A host-supplied derived dataset remains an alternative.
query_table_requests.performance: Keep both stages on the server and limit stages/group cardinality. Intermediate relation semantics must preserve grain and row lineage.

query_table_requests.title: Time buckets and aligned period comparisons
query_table_requests.gap: Relative bounds already exist upstream. Local-hour/date bucketing is not in the initial server profile; cohort comparison requires manual datasets or several requests.
query_table_requests.proposal: Expose tested timezone-aware time bucket fields/functions and current/previous or before/after period selection under one evaluation clock. Define gaps, unequal durations, civil versus elapsed time and rate denominators.
query_table_requests.performance: Lower relative ranges to indexed timestamp bounds; reuse period scans and existing daily facts. A formatting timezone does not change grouping timezone.

query_table_requests.title: Named measures and shared reductions at one grain
query_table_requests.gap: Two measures are paired for scatter, but general named measure bundles are absent; a metric batch compiles one separate statement per metric.
query_table_requests.proposal: Allow a grouped result to return named measures such as calls, failures, rate, timed calls, duration and price coverage. Reuse common input projections and aggregate leaves when possible, preserving a coherent snapshot.
examples: Failure rate with numerator and denominator
query_table_requests.performance: An HTTP batch is not necessarily one scan. Preserve Pharos cube rewrites and weighted sums rather than rescanning raw calls for every small preview.

query_table_requests.title: Scalar percentiles and explicit precision
query_table_requests.gap: Box summaries expose fixed quartiles; scalar MEDIAN is present only in Go and absent from the core aggregate set; arbitrary PERCENTILE is missing.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add typed median/percentile reductions usable in formulas and named measures, with shared TS/server conformance. Advertise exact or approximate algorithms, numeric sample count and precision.
query_table_requests.performance: Exact ordering can be expensive and existing sum/min/max cubes cannot reconstruct quantiles. Offer sketches only with explicit approximation semantics.

query_table_requests.title: Typed drillthrough and bounded evidence
query_table_requests.gap: Bucket inspection exists; a clicked histogram bin does not carry a bin-range selection, and there is no standardized selection-to-source or exemplar contract.
query_table_requests.proposal: Extend inspection with metric identity, typed group keys, selected range or mark and resolved query context. Provide a host resolver for contributing rows and bounded exemplar hydration; preserve source IDs and evidence locators.
examples: A correction next to its earlier response
Specific calls behind a failure ranking
The sessions inside an outlier bin
query_table_requests.performance: Fetch a few exemplars lazily or in one bounded batch. Do not attach full transcript content to every aggregate bucket.

query_table_requests.title: A reusable compact plot presentation
query_table_requests.gap: Standalone MetricCard and headless useAggregations are already exported. The chart is internally tied to card chrome and normal axis/legend sizing.
query_table_requests.proposal: Offer a plot-only or compact presentation using the same computation, marks, color resolver and units as full views. Make compact label/legend/detail budgets explicit and expose a documented consumption API.
query_table_requests.performance: Rendering remains bounded by marks and labels and should never trigger a second computation for presentation-only edits.

query_table_requests.title: Coverage freshness clocks and execution budgets
query_table_requests.gap: The v2 compiler and integration guide already specify shared clock/snapshot identity and host-owned response metadata. Pharos has not adopted the contract; freshness, moving-window cache expiry and source coverage need an end-to-end agreement.
query_table_requests.proposal: Adopt and finish the existing contract with final input/sample/group counts, truncation/precision, host data revision, echoed as-of clock and cache expiry for moving windows. Carry host-provided source freshness/coverage separately from computational exactness. Enforce deadlines/cancellation and explicit rejected plans.
examples: Fast reloads with fresh relative windows
query_table_requests.performance: Cache on data and definition revision plus resolved clock/window; LIMIT only bounds output. Host-level candidate scheduling should prioritize visible previews.

query_table_requests.title: Portable execution profiles and conformance fixtures
query_table_requests.gap: The new Go planner emits PostgreSQL casts/functions. Pharos runs SQLite and its own map executor; v2 is not available by changing frontend dependencies.
query_table_requests.proposal: Provide a dialect-neutral validated execution plan or a documented adapter seam plus portable semantic fixtures. Add a SQLite profile where appropriate, or let Pharos implement the same negotiated v2 contract without pretending every function is portable.
examples: All new all-matching formulas and distributions in Pharos
query_table_requests.performance: Retain SQLite indexes, FTS and cube routing. Hosts own actual execution, deadlines and prepared views; conformance checks cover nulls, errors, lazy branches and numeric precision.

query_table_requests.title: An indexed search predicate seam
query_table_requests.gap: Library text search operates outside QueryState and reduces hits to workspaces; agent messages are not a Query Table root. Full-population regex metric inputs remain out of scope.
query_table_requests.proposal: Let a host advertise a persisted, typed indexed-search predicate/source that participates in the same counts, groups and cache identity as ordinary filters. Define matched-row versus parent-membership semantics and bounded-search coverage; Pharos supplies FTS and excerpt hydration.
examples: Agent confusion in the last seven days
query_table_requests.performance: Apply role and message-time constraints to the match population. Do not replace indexed search with a regex scan of every transcript or filter workspace activity dates as if they were message dates.

query_table_requests.title: Grouped time series and heatmap presentation
query_table_requests.gap: Line charts are one chronological series; two-key output has a pivot/table route, but no explicit heatmap or shared stacked-series chart contract.
query_table_requests.proposal: Support time × category series with explicit missing/zero semantics, stacked or grouped marks, stable colors and an exact remainder; add a bounded two-key heatmap. Share full and compact renderers.
query_table_requests.performance: Bound time buckets and categories; preserve totals when folding an additive remainder. Do not smooth missing observations or sum rates across categories.

query_table_requests.title: Bounded expansion of set-valued dimensions
query_table_requests.gap: Arrays support membership filtering but are not admitted server row expressions; grouping a host list is not grouping each member.
query_table_requests.proposal: Offer an explicit explode-members stage or a normalized host relation with declared parent identity. Define event-count versus membership-count measures and restrict simultaneous expansions to prevent accidental cross products.
examples: All files touched by a work
query_table_requests.performance: Index normalized members or materialize them during ingestion. Carry distinct parent IDs to avoid multiplying usage or costs across memberships.

query_table_requests.title: Editable bookmark metadata with stable IDs
query_table_requests.gap: SavedQuery carries name, timestamp and QueryState. StorageAdapter has saveNamed/delete, but no stable-ID update for name/description/order or discovery across dataset namespaces.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add optional stable-ID bookmark updates for title, description and user order, and a host-controlled way to enumerate relevant bookmarks across dataset namespaces. Keep queries as canonical storage and preserve existing adapters.
examples: Rename and describe a collected card
Keep one query identity across surfaces
query_table_requests.performance: This is storage/API work rather than metric computation. Metadata changes should not invalidate arithmetic or recreate saved IDs.

query_table_requests.title: Registered relationships with explicit cardinality
query_table_requests.gap: The host can already supply a joined SourceSQL, but users cannot compose registered dataset relationships.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider approved relation joins or semi-joins with declared grain and cardinality, not arbitrary SQL. Provide fanout-aware measures and source lineage.
query_table_requests.performance: Prejoin recurring relationships in Pharos first; index join keys and prevent multiplication of already-aggregated facts.

query_table_requests.title: Ordered partition functions
query_table_requests.gap: Formula context rejects windows and source order is not exposed as an analytical operation.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider LAG/LEAD, first/last-by-order, running counts and elapsed differences over a declared partition and stable event ordering.
query_table_requests.performance: Use partition/order indexes and bound the queried streams. Filter-after-window semantics may require earlier events outside a visible time window.

query_table_requests.title: Sessionization and event episode or funnel recipes
query_table_requests.gap: Recovery and verification episodes do not exist as generic metric inputs.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider deterministic, bounded sessionization and ordered-pattern extraction over typed events. Keep definitions explicit and let hosts supply materialized episode rows.
query_table_requests.performance: Repeated homepage requests should query episode facts updated on ingestion rather than recompute every transcript sequence. Episode-boundary definitions are often domain-specific.

query_table_requests.title: Interval union overlap and concurrency
query_table_requests.gap: SUM(duration) cannot compute wall time for parallel activity; no interval transform is exposed.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider typed interval-union length, overlap episodes and time-bucket occupancy as optional reducers or prepared host facts.
query_table_requests.performance: Sweep ordered interval endpoints rather than join every interval pair. Report open/missing endpoints and never substitute summed durations for elapsed time.

query_table_requests.title: Co-occurrence and association over prepared sets
query_table_requests.gap: File pairs and workflow motifs require pair/sequence creation and normalized marginal counts.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider bounded association reducers over prepared membership or edge datasets: support count, joint frequency and explicit marginals for lift. Keep pair generation and semantic labels in the host initially.
query_table_requests.performance: Pair expansion can be quadratic; cap set size, use incremental sparse counts and minimum support before ranking.

query_table_requests.title: Named scenario parameters and aligned variants
query_table_requests.gap: Literal arithmetic can already calculate a scenario once rates and inputs are fields, but no reusable parameter bundle or named variant output exists.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider typed saved parameters with units and several labeled variants over the same prepared population. Hosts supply rates and billing data.
query_table_requests.performance: Reuse workload projections across scenarios. Keep parameters out of display labels and external lookups out of expression execution.

query_table_requests.title: An optional result renderer registration seam
query_table_requests.gap: Current chart families do not render transcript excerpts, event paths, parallel lanes or trees.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider host-rendered result kinds with typed validated payloads, inspect callbacks, theme access and compact/full variants. Avoid building every domain-specific cover into the core library.
query_table_requests.performance: Bound nodes/edges/excerpts, preserve query identity and defer hydration. Keep nonserializable callbacks out of saved-query state.

query_table_requests.title: A batch scheduler for heterogeneous previews
query_table_requests.gap: A v2 metric batch shares one WHERE, while a carousel pool spans filters, windows and datasets.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider a reusable headless runner for several query plans with concurrency caps, cancellation, partial completion, memoization and visible-first priorities; the host may implement this without changing QueryState.
examples: Eligibility checks for a large suggestion pool
query_table_requests.performance: Group compatible candidates to share work, cache on explicit revisions/window anchors and fetch only a selected preview subset. Backend scan fusion is distinct from HTTP request batching.

query_table_requests.title: Semantic interpretation inside metric expressions
query_table_requests.gap: Confusion loops, decisions, examples and scope changes require meaning extraction.
query_table_requests.proposal: Keep semantic extraction, embedding similarity and evidence-backed labels in Pharos. Query Table should consume their versioned annotations and indexed similarity result rows.
query_table_requests.performance: Do expensive extraction incrementally outside interactive queries; expose provenance and uncertain classifications.

query_table_requests.title: Automatic causal or quality judgments
query_table_requests.gap: Recorded outcomes and correlations cannot establish model superiority, productivity or cause.
query_table_requests.proposal: Offer explicit cohorts, denominators and underlying evidence. Keep domain scoring and recommendation ranking outside generic arithmetic; avoid a universal opaque success score.
query_table_requests.performance: Matched populations and statistical uncertainty are host/domain work; charting cannot solve confounding.

query_table_requests.title: Arbitrary SQL or recursive graph analytics in saved metrics
query_table_requests.gap: These would widen a deliberately allowlisted expression API into a general database language.
query_table_requests.proposal: Prefer registered sources, narrow relational stages and host-produced lineage closures or episode facts. Do not add raw user SQL, arbitrary recursive queries or unrestricted transcript regex as a homepage shortcut.
query_table_requests.performance: Unbounded graph/pair/text scans are poor interactive workloads and require host access and resource boundaries.

query_table_requests.title: Provider pricing billing or carbon models owned by Query Table
query_table_requests.gap: These require domain rate tables, assumptions and sometimes external/user data.
query_table_requests.proposal: Keep price books, billing inputs and energy models in Pharos. Query Table handles typed arithmetic, variants and visualization over prepared fields.
query_table_requests.performance: Version inputs and materialize compatible pricing components. Do not fetch providers as metric side effects.

query_table_requests.title: Automatically create database indexes or materializations for every saved formula
query_table_requests.gap: Expression execution does not imply a good database index, and definitions can change.
query_table_requests.proposal: Let the host measure plans and opt into projections, generated values, sketches or expression indexes. A core plan/explain hook is reasonable; automatic schema writes are not the default.
query_table_requests.performance: Account for ingestion/write cost, data volume and definition revisions; avoid proliferating expensive indexes for speculative cards.
